data.title: Grayscale’s Zcash ETF plans 3-for-1 split after $233 million inflow surge
data.description:
Grayscale's Zcash ETF is moving to undergo a 3-for-1 share split less than a month after it began trading.

At market close on Sept. 28, ZCSH shareholders will receive two additional shares for every share they own, according to a Friday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. New shares will be distributed after market close on Sept. 29, and split-adjusted trading begins on Sept. 30.

Investors have cumulatively poured more than $233 million into ZCSH since launching on Aug. 25, including a $46.6 million day on Wednesday and more than $112 million on Sept. 8.

The fund held around $890 million in net assets and generated more than $11 billion in cumulative trading volume as of Sept. 17.

This comes as Zcash's native ZEC token climbed as high as $1,521 early Friday, marking what would be considered a new effective all-time high.

ZEC mining rush

The rally has also drawn waves of additional compute power to the Zcash network. Its estimated solrate, which is essentially equivalent to its network hashrate, has climbed from around 25 GSol/s in late August to just under 32 GSol/s, an increase of nearly 28%, according to Zcash Info.

Mining difficulty has risen alongside it to about 291 million, also a record high.

The increased competition, however, is starting to weigh on revenue generated by each machine. Earlier this month, estimated gross revenue for Bitmain's Z15 Pro has already slipped below its late-August level despite ZEC's price rally, as the network needed to divide rewards among more computing power.

data.title: US CDC works on standard definition for measles deaths as cases rise
data.description:
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to develop a standardized case definition for measles deaths, the agency said Friday, as the outbreak grows across the country.

Here are the details:

  • The CDC reported 3,471 confirmed measles cases in the United States as of September 17, up from 3,294 a week earlier, with no deaths recorded for 2026 in its national tally.

  • The Pennsylvania Department of Health earlier this week reported two more measles-associated deaths, both in unvaccinated individuals, bringing the state's total outbreak-linked fatalities to four.

  • The CDC, however, has not included the deaths after the agency shifted to using mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics for its national measles death count, moving away from its previous reliance on state health departments — a change that has drawn scrutiny.

  • The Pennsylvania health department on Thursday sought emergency support from the CDC to tackle its measles outbreak, on the condition that the agency recognize four measles-associated deaths reported by the state.

  • The CDC said it would update its reporting as more information becomes available and relevant reviews are completed.

  • On Wednesday, the US Senate health committee's Republican chairman blamed the Trump administration's approach to vaccines for recent measles deaths in Pennsylvania.

data.title: Polymarket and Yahoo Finance end prediction market pact
data.description:
Yahoo Finance ended a partnership with Polymarket that allowed it to use Polymarket data for a prediction market hub on its website, according to a media report on Friday.

The companies forged the agreement last November. At the time, Polymarket said its probability data for key economic, government, and market outcomes would be paired with related news, quotes, and analysis from Yahoo Finance and its partners. "By combining trusted data with in-depth analysis, the hub will empower investors to make smarter, more strategic prediction market investments," Polymarket said  in a social media post.

The predictions market hub was removed in April, and the partnership agreement ended, Bloomberg News reported.  A spokesperson told Bloomberg, "That specific agreement ended, but Polymarket continues to be an advertising partner across Yahoo, and we’re open to similar types of partnerships."

Polymarket and its rival, Kalshi , have entered agreements with a number of news websites, broadcasters, and publications. For example, Polymarket entered an agreement with News Corp.'s Dow Jones division, which publishes the Wall Street Journal and Barron's. Kalshi has inked partnerships with Warner Bros. Discovery's CNN, Versant Media Group's CNBC, and Fox Corp. .

data.title: CrowdStrike Gets Higher Targets From BofA, Stephens — Guardian And Expanding AI Security Market Drive Analyst Confidence
data.description:
Key points:
  • BofA raised its CRWD target to $260 from $230 and kept a 'Neutral' rating.
  • BofA said Falcon Guardian is “setting the industry standard” for AI detection and response.
  • Stephens raised its target to $280 from $260 and maintained an Overweight rating.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (CRWD) drew price-target hikes from BofA and Stephens following a string of AI-focused announcements at its annual flagship cybersecurity conference, Fal.Con, according to TheFly.

BofA raised its price target on CRWD stock to $260 from $230 while maintaining a ‘Neutral’ rating, saying the announcements have “cemented” CrowdStrike’s position at the forefront of AI security, per TheFly. The firm singled out Falcon Guardian, saying the product is setting the industry standard for AI detection and response.

Stephens raised its target on the stock to $280 from $260 and maintained an ‘Overweight’ rating. The firm cited an expanding AI-driven cybersecurity market, continued benefits from industry consolidation and CrowdStrike’s position as “one of a select number of strategic cybersecurity platform providers," according to TheFly.

Falcon Guardian Takes Center Stage At Fal.Con

CrowdStrike introduced Falcon Guardian at Fal.Con as an AI Detection and Response platform designed to monitor and control AI agents while they are running. It can discover AI agents, monitor their actions, enforce access controls, and detect malicious or compromised behavior across endpoints, cloud, software-as-a-service (SaaS), and browser environments.

The cybersecurity technology company also expanded its OpenAI partnership, bringing Guardian protection to ChatGPT Codex agents while integrating GPT-5.6 Cyber into parts of the Falcon platform for cybersecurity risk assessment and analysis.

CrowdStrike Broadens Its AI Security Stack

At the Fal.Con event, CrowdStrike also expanded Falcon across Google Cloud’s enterprise AI ecosystem, including Guardian integration through Google Agent Gateway and new integrations with Gemini Enterprise for security operations and AI governance.

The company separately introduced an Agentic Identity Provider to establish trusted identities and control access for AI agents, while its new SafeMind system combines offensive and defensive AI models for cybersecurity.

Retail Sentiment Around CRWD Stock

Retail sentiment around CRWD turned ‘bearish’ on Stocktwits, amid high message volumes. CrowdStrike shares were trading more than 3% lower on Friday at the time of this writing.

So far this year, CRWD stock has more than doubled, surging over 108%. In comparison, the First Trust NASDAQ Cybersecurity ETF (CIBR), which holds CrowdStrike shares, has risen more than 40% over the same period.

data.title: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Preferred Networks Form Capital and Business Alliance
data.description:
TOKYO, Sept 18, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. (MHI) and Preferred Networks, Inc. (PFN) today announced that they entered into a capital and business alliance agreement on August 31, 2026. In June 2026, the two companies announced an initial business alliance(1) to jointly develop cutting-edge AI technologies to enhance the intelligence and autonomy of machinery and systems across mission-critical domains, including social infrastructure and national security. This capital and business alliance agreement establishes a robust cooperative framework to advance MHI and PFN's joint development over the medium to long term. Under the agreement, MHI will underwrite shares issued by PFN through a third-party allotment and invest a total of 10 billion yen in PFN, accelerating the joint development, subject to the completion of all necessary procedures, including approvals at PFN's general meeting of shareholders.

Amid increasingly complex societal challenges, including shifting global dynamics, labor shortages, and aging social infrastructure, demand is growing to deploy advanced AI in mission-critical domains such as social infrastructure and national security. These domains require high reliability and rapid responsiveness to enhance resilience and ensure safety and security. Applying AI in mission-critical domains requires a deep understanding and control of AI mechanisms, securely integrated with field operations, equipment and control systems. Furthermore, to ensure that Japan can proactively and stably leverage AI technologies independently from the external environment, accumulating AI technologies, data, and operational expertise domestically is increasingly vital.

Deploying AI effectively under these conditions requires deep expertise in operational sites, equipment and control systems in mission-critical domains, alongside a technological foundation that supports everything from AI development to deployment and operation.

MHI has provided and operated resilient, safe, and secure machinery and systems for decades across sectors such as social infrastructure, aerospace, defense, and space. The company has brought technologies and expertise in design, manufacturing, control, simulation and maintenance, along with data linked to onsite situations and conditions, backed by operational field data and deep customer trust.

PFN internally develops a full stack of technologies for AI, ranging from AI chips, computing infrastructure, and generative AI foundation models to products and solutions. Centered on homegrown technologies, PFN has deployed safe and sustainable AI technologies across diverse industrial environments.

Through this capital and business alliance, the two companies will combine their technologies and expertise to accelerate joint R&D and real-world deployment of intelligent, autonomous machinery and systems for social infrastructure and national security, where high reliability and rapid responsiveness are required. As partners moving forward together, MHI and PFN share a mindset of being agile, fast, and constantly evolving without being bound by existing frameworks. Together, the two companies aim to create new value and contribute to the maintenance and development of a safe and secure society.

Comment from Eisaku Ito, President and CEO, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd.:

"PFN's commitment to implementing cutting-edge, domestically developed AI technologies across hardware and software deeply resonates with the spirit of craftsmanship that flows through MHI. Deploying AI in mission-critical domains is one of the top-priority issues for strengthening societal resilience, and we have built these values as we move toward development and commercialization through our joint research and business alliance.

MHI advocates for 'ITO' (Innovative Total Optimization) and is working on total optimization and domain expansion with unprecedented speed. This capital and business alliance with PFN aligns with ITO, in that it advances total optimization and maximizes the strengths of both companies to expand into new domains. We view this alliance as an essential step toward building a truly safe and secure society, and we will dedicate our full efforts to the implementation of more innovative next-generation infrastructure than ever before."

Comment from Daisuke Okanohara, CEO, Preferred Networks, Inc.:

"Deploying AI in mission-critical domains is a complex challenge on a global scale. To make AI practical on the ground, we must go beyond model performance - we must address field-specific constraints, ensure reliability, real-time responsiveness and continuous operability, while optimizing hardware and software as a whole. Through our joint research, MHI and PFN have aligned on this perspective while advancing efforts toward practical implementation.

Under this capital and business alliance, we will deeply connect MHI's decades of expertise in field operations, equipment, control systems and safe operations with PFN's vertically integrated technologies - from AI chips to foundation models - we will deliver achievements that neither company could accomplish alone, bolstering social safety and industrial competitiveness."

(1) Please see the following press release regarding the business alliance:

https://www.mhi.com/news/260602.html

About Preferred Networks

Guided by its mission to "Make the real world computable and create the future together," Preferred Networks, Inc. (PFN) develops advanced software and hardware technologies through a vertically integrated approach spanning the entire AI value chain-from AI chips and computing infrastructure to generative AI foundation models and solutions across a wide range of industries. Founded in 2014 in Tokyo, PFN currently develops and delivers the MN-Core(TM) series of AI processors, the PFCP(TM) cloud platform for AI computing, and the Japan-developed generative AI foundation model PLaMo(TM). https://www.preferred.jp/en/

About MHI Group

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) Group is one of the world's leading industrial groups, spanning energy, smart infrastructure, industrial machinery, aerospace and defense. MHI Group combines cutting-edge technology with deep experience to deliver innovative, integrated solutions that help to realize a carbon neutral world, improve the quality of life and ensure a safer world. For more information, please visit www.mhi.com or follow our insights and stories on spectra.mhi.com.

Source: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI)

data.title: Combiflam MS Cream Creates Relaxation Zone For Lalbaugcha Raja Devotees
data.description:
Returning for its second consecutive year, the Charan Vandana activation offers complimentary leg massage chairs to devotees waiting in the general darshan queue at Mumbai’s Lalbaugcha Raja

Combiflam MS Cream has brought back its Charan Vandana activation at Mumbai’s Lalbaugcha Raja for the second consecutive year, using an on-ground utility-led experience to offer devotees a place to rest during their wait for darshan.

Running from September 14 to 23, the activation has been integrated into the general darshan queue and features six complimentary leg massage chairs. The experience is aimed at devotees spending extended periods on their feet while waiting to visit the Ganesh pandal.

The initiative connects the brand’s pain-relief positioning with a specific consumer need arising during the festival. Instead of limiting its presence to conventional festive branding, Combiflam MS Cream is using the activation to provide a service at the point where physical fatigue and discomfort are likely to be experienced.

Nupur Gurbaxani, Director Marketing, Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India, says, “For many people, visiting Lalbaugcha Raja is a deeply meaningful experience. The journey often involves long hours of waiting and can be physically demanding. At Sanofi Consumer Healthcare, we believe care should be accessible wherever people need it. While pain and discomfort may sometimes accompany the pursuit of what matters most to us, they should not become barriers to our dreams and aspirations.

“Through the Charan Vandana initiative, Combiflam MS Cream is helping bring care closer to people at their point of need, enabling greater comfort during one of Mumbai’s most cherished celebrations. We hope this initiative provides relief and support to devotees, helping them focus on the experience that brought them there in the first place.”

The return of Charan Vandana also reflects how brands are increasingly approaching large cultural gatherings as opportunities for utility-led engagement. At Lalbaugcha Raja, where devotees can spend long periods waiting in queues, the activation places the brand within the consumer journey through a service directly connected with its category.

By returning for a second year, Combiflam MS Cream is extending the association beyond a one-off festive intervention, positioning Charan Vandana as a recurring experiential touchpoint during Ganesh Chaturthi.

data.title: L&T Semiconductor, Tata Electronics Partner On Chip Fabrication, Packaging
data.description:
L&T Semiconductor Technologies Limited (LTSCT) and Tata Electronics have entered into a strategic partnership to jointly develop and manufacture semiconductor products in India, as the companies seek to build domestic capabilities spanning chip design, fabrication and advanced packaging.

Under the partnership, the companies will explore fabrication and packaging opportunities for LTSCT's existing and future chip products using Tata Electronics' range of semiconductor manufacturing processes and packaging technologies, according to a joint statement on Friday.

The collaboration will also cover design-to-fabrication optimisation, with the companies seeking to improve chip designs for efficient manufacturing at scale.

The partnership targets semiconductor applications across automotive, industrial, communications, security and intelligent-edge markets, with an emphasis on serving both Indian and global customers.

"Semiconductor leadership will increasingly be defined not just by design breakthroughs but by the ability to industrialise those designs through advanced packaging and manufacturing," LTSCT Chief Executive Sandeep Kumar said.

LTSCT, the semiconductor arm of engineering conglomerate Larsen & Toubro, operates as a fabless semiconductor company, while Tata Electronics is building capabilities in semiconductor fabrication, packaging and testing in India.

Tata Electronics CEO and Managing Director Randhir Thakur said the partnership would combine LTSCT's semiconductor design and engineering capabilities with Tata Electronics' manufacturing, packaging and testing infrastructure.

The companies said the alliance supports India's push to develop a domestic semiconductor ecosystem and increase value addition in the country under the government's semiconductor programme.

data.title: TCS, Tata Chemicals, Tata Steel to Tata Motors PV - Tata Group stock lost 46,600 crores in a single day
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 18 -- Shares of Tata Group companies came under heavy selling pressure in Friday's trade, September 18, with the combined market capitalisation of several listed group firms eroding by Rs.46,600 crore.

The sell-off came as an unprecedented boardroom revolt at Tata Sons pushed the 158-year-old conglomerate into a high-stakes governance crisis, while uncertainty over the holding company's potential listing added to investor concerns.

The sharp losses followed a dramatic turn of events at Tata Sons, the group's holding company. The board, on Thursday, asked Chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran to continue for another five years and approved a potential public listing of the company by a majority vote, according to a Tata Sons statement.

The developments came after the RBI refused to exempt Tata Sons from a listing requirement last week. Chandrasekaran, widely known as Chandra, agreed to extend his tenure just weeks after announcing plans to step down in February.

However, the governance uncertainty escalated shortly after the announcement. Tata Trusts, the controlling shareholder of Tata Sons, called the board's decision to extend Chandrasekaran's tenure "illegal" in a separate statement.

The Trusts, a group of 13 charitable organisations, had also said late Thursday that they had not agreed to a listing of Tata Sons. They added that the company's board was required to explore all available options, further deepening uncertainty over the group's future direction.

Separately, Tata Trusts said Shapoorji Pallonji Group, Tata Sons' second-largest shareholder, had proposed monetising part of its 18.4% stake through a two-tranche buyout that would yield at least $2.61 billion over 18 months.

The boardroom showdown comes at a challenging time for Tata Group, with several of its major businesses facing operational and financial headwinds. Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) is dealing with a slowing European market, while Air India continues to grapple with heavy losses following a fatal crash and geopolitical disruptions.

Meanwhile, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), the group's flagship technology company, is facing challenges in reigniting growth, Bloomberg reported.

About Rs.46,634 crore was erased from the combined market value of listed Tata Group companies on Friday, according to LiveMint calculations based on exchange data.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) saw the biggest erosion in market capitalisation among the Tata Group stocks, losing around Rs.29,550 crore as its share price fell 3.88% in Friday's trade. It was followed by Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, which shed about Rs.3,804 crore in market value after the stock declined 3.40%.

Tata Steel lost around Rs.2,154 crore in market capitalisation as its shares fell 1%, while Tata Chemicals saw a sharp decline of 11%, wiping out approximately Rs.1,942 crore from its market value. Tata Consumer Products lost around Rs.1,725 crore, with the stock falling 1.75%, while Tata Technologies declined 4.78%, eroding nearly Rs.1,402 crore in market capitalisation.

Tata Investment Corporation saw its market value decline by around Rs.838 crore as shares fell 2.36%, followed by Voltas, which lost approximately Rs.779 crore after declining 2.12%.

Tata Elxsi shed around Rs.692 crore in market capitalisation, with its shares falling 3.40%, while Titan Company lost approximately Rs.3,748 crore despite a relatively modest 0.88% decline in its share price.

(With inputs from Bloomberg)

data.title: India’s Semiconductor Opportunity Lies In Innovation: Infosys SVP
data.description:
Vikram Meghal says AI, supply-chain shifts and system-level scaling are creating a new demand window for India’s semiconductor ecosystem

India is facing a “once-in-a-generation demand window” in semiconductors as artificial intelligence (AI), geopolitical supply-chain shifts and changes in chip design reshape the global industry, according to Infosys Senior Vice President Vikram Meghal.

Speaking at Semicon India 2026, Meghal said India needs to move beyond engineering capabilities and take greater ownership of complete systems and products.

Meghal said the traditional semiconductor pipeline is being disrupted as workloads, particularly those driven by AI,determine how chips are designed. He also pointed to the shift from Moore’s Law towards system-level scaling as another structural change affecting the industry.

AI Reshapes Chip Demand

AI is creating a major new source of semiconductor demand, with data-centre spending expected to reach USD 6.7 trillion over the next few years, Meghal said. Around half of this spending is expected to go towards compute, memory and networking chips.

According to Meghal, the industry is moving towards a model in which workloads drive chip design rather than chips determining the nature of the workload. This shift is creating opportunities for countries that can participate not only in chip engineering but also in developing products and systems around specific applications.

Meghal identified three major demand fronts for India: “Made for India”, “Engineered in India” and “Invent in India”.

Three Demand Fronts

The “Made for India” opportunity is linked to the localisation of products and components for the domestic market. Meghal said mobile phone localisation has already begun, but domestic content currently stands at only 23 per cent, leaving room for the market to expand significantly over the next four to five years.

The second opportunity is “Engineered in India”, where the country can build on its existing engineering and research and development capabilities. Meghal said engineering, research and development spending is expected to grow 1.8 times from current levels in the coming years.

However, Meghal said the larger opportunity lies in “Invent in India”, particularly as the global market for custom chips expands. Application-specific silicon could create opportunities for Indian companies to capture more of the value associated with innovation and product ownership.

From Engineering To Innovation

Meghal said India has already built significant capabilities in engineering at scale, but the next phase should involve developing products for global markets from India.

“So far, we have just been capturing the engineered-in-India value. Now, there is a potential for global products to capture the innovation value and start looking at inventing in India itself. That's really where we will do justice to the decades of investment that we have done in building this ecosystem,” he said.

Meghal urged companies to adopt what he described as “strategic patience” when making investments in the semiconductor sector, given the scale and time horizon involved in building capabilities.

Meghal also called for a stronger product mindset, greater attention to regulatory compliance and efforts to own the entire technology stack rather than concentrating only on the silicon.

data.title: Odisha Wants To Build A Complete Semiconductor Ecosystem: CM Majhi
data.description:
The state is targeting investments across SiC, GaN, advanced packaging, wafers, materials and equipment, backed by additional fiscal incentives

Odisha is seeking to build a complete semiconductor ecosystem spanning compound chips, advanced packaging, wafers, materials and equipment, as the eastern Indian state looks to attract investments beyond individual manufacturing plants, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said.

“It means a full ecosystem, not only limited to a plant. This is cluster-based industrialisation with one anchor investment attracting the next,” Majhi said.

Odisha has approved five semiconductor projects involving a combined investment of Rs 10,899 crore, expected to create more than 4,500 direct and 16,000 indirect jobs, he said.

The projects include SiCSem's silicon carbide (SiC) semiconductor fab and packaging facility and an advanced glass substrate packaging facility by Heterogeneous Integration Packaging Solutions (HIPS/3DGS).

The state is also looking to expand into upstream parts of the supply chain. Discussions are underway to convert an Intel-3DGS memorandum of understanding into a large-scale advanced glass substrate and packaging investment, while Sancode Technologies is being considered for a second-phase packaging facility, Majhi said.

SiCSem is exploring a second phase combining SiC and gallium nitride (GaN) fabrication and packaging, while QuadQuantum is exploring a raw-material SiC wafer facility, he added.

Separately, RIR Power Electronics has completed installation of SiC epitaxial wafer manufacturing reactors at its Bhubaneswar facility and is expected to begin commercial production soon, Majhi said.

Odisha will provide an additional 25% state fiscal support on eligible capital expenditure for India Semiconductor Mission-approved projects, including semiconductor equipment, chemicals, gases and materials, under its alignment with the Centre's Semicon 2.0 programme, he said.

The state is also setting up a Rs 452 crore National Industry Co-Development Hub on Integrated Power Electronics at IIT Bhubaneswar, jointly funded by the Centre, Odisha, the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and industry partners.

“Odisha is uniquely positioned to emerge as India's leading hub for compound semiconductors, advanced packaging and semiconductor ecosystem manufacturing,” Majhi said.

data.title: Bank Of Maharashtra’s $500 Mn Overseas Bond Gets Nearly 3x Subscription
data.description:
The public sector lender makes its debut in international debt markets with a five-year dollar bond aimed at funding business growth

Bank of Maharashtra has raised USD 500 million through its first-ever overseas bond issuance, with the five-year dollar-denominated bond receiving nearly three times the subscription from international investors.

The issue marks the public sector lender’s entry into international debt markets and was completed in a single tranche. The bonds are senior unsecured notes issued through the bank’s International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) banking unit under its USD 500 million medium-term note programme.

The proceeds will be used to meet funding requirements at the bank’s India head office and foreign branches, as well as for general corporate purposes.

Bond Draws Strong Global Demand

The strong investor response allowed Bank of Maharashtra to tighten the pricing of the bond from its initial guidance.

The bonds carry a coupon of 6.112 per cent and were priced at a spread of 130 basis points over the five-year US Treasury. The final spread was 25 basis points lower than the initial guidance of 155 basis points.

The bonds are rated BBB by S&P and BBB- by Fitch Ratings. The issuance also comes under the Reserve Bank of India’s concessional swap window, which helps reduce the cost of hedging foreign currency exposure.

Indian Banks Step Up Dollar Borrowing

Bank of Maharashtra’s debut comes amid increased activity by Indian banks in the international debt market. State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank and Union Bank of India have also raised funds through dollar bonds this year.

Indian banks have raised around USD 13 billion through dollar bonds since June, when the Reserve Bank of India introduced the swap window to support foreign currency borrowing.

The latest issuance gives Bank of Maharashtra access to a wider pool of international investors while diversifying its funding sources. The bank said the strong order book reflects demand for its paper as it enters the international debt market after more than nine decades of operations.

data.title: BEL CMD Calls For 1-2 Year Roadmap To Plug India’s EW Gaps
data.description:
BEL CMD Manoj Jain identifies radar coverage, spectrum awareness, radar protection and distributed sensing as immediate priorities

Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL) Chairman and Managing Director Manoj Jain has called for a one-to-two-year roadmap to address gaps in India’s electronic warfare (EW) capabilities, with greater focus on radar awareness, spectrum sensing and protection of existing assets. Speaking at a press conference organised by the Synergia Foundation, Jain said India needs to move quickly on these capabilities and begin field-level deployments while building technologies that can be integrated with existing defence systems.

Jain identified four broad areas that require immediate attention: improving radar awareness and coverage, strengthening spectrum awareness, protecting radar assets through solutions such as decoys, and deploying distributed, miniaturised spectrum-sensing systems. He also called for a common national interfacing standard to enable sensors from different suppliers to work together.

Radar Awareness And Coverage

Jain said India needs to address gaps in its radar inventory and improve its ability to monitor emerging threats, including aircraft equipped with stealth technologies. He pointed to technologies such as bi-static and multi-static radar systems as areas that need to be developed and moved towards field-level deployment.

The BEL chief said a one-to-two-year roadmap should be prepared for these capabilities, with the objective of translating the technologies into products that can be inducted into the inventory. He also highlighted spectrum awareness as a key requirement for electronic warfare, particularly as adversaries can employ capabilities aimed at disrupting or degrading radar systems.

Jain added India needs stronger wideband radar capabilities and systems that can operate differently during peacetime and periods of heightened operational stress.

Protecting Existing Radar Assets

Another priority identified by Jain is the protection of radar assets already deployed by the armed forces. He said several existing radar assets do not have sufficient protection against attacks and that solutions need to be progressively added to the inventory.

Jain specifically referred to decoys as one capability that needs to be developed and deployed rapidly. He said such systems could form part of efforts to protect radar assets in an environment where electronic warfare and other threats are becoming increasingly important. The focus, he said, should not only be on developing new systems but also on improving the survivability of existing assets through additional protective capabilities.

Distributed Spectrum Sensing

Jain also called for the development of intermediate EW sensing capabilities between ground-based systems and high-altitude or space-based assets. He said altitude can provide an advantage in electronic-warfare sensing and identified the need for additional platforms that can improve spectrum awareness.

He suggested that such capabilities could potentially be deployed using drones or other intermediate platforms. The objective would be to create miniaturised spectrum-sensing devices that can be distributed and networked to provide greater awareness of activity across the electromagnetic spectrum.

According to Jain, building these capabilities should form part of the immediate one-to-two-year roadmap, with products subsequently brought into the defence inventory.

Common Architecture For Sensor Integration

Jain said developing individual sensors would not be sufficient unless the systems can be integrated into a common architecture. He called for a central-level architecture and a national interfacing standard that can allow sensors supplied by different Indian companies to communicate with one another.

Under such a framework, suppliers could build systems that comply with a common interface, enabling them to be networked more easily and allowing information from multiple sensors to be brought together.

Jain said integration also needs to address security risks. Connecting multiple sensors and systems could create vulnerabilities if adequate security layers are not built into the architecture. He said the challenge would be to achieve integration while maintaining appropriate separation and security across the network.

Collaboration Across Defence Ecosystem

Jain also stressed the role of collaboration between academia, startups and established defence companies in developing niche technologies. He said electronic warfare increasingly involves multiple technologies, including advanced sensors, photonics and quantum sensing, making cooperation across different layers of the ecosystem important.

He cautioned against developing technologies only from an individual product perspective, arguing that different components need to ultimately contribute to an end-to-end solution. Such collaboration, he said, would also help integrate newer technologies with legacy command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (C4ISR) systems already deployed by the armed forces.

Jain further called for greater emphasis on building intellectual property within India, saying indigenous IP would help the country transition more quickly to next-generation defence technologies.

data.title: Dollar jumps against yen as BOJ dissent clouds rate-hike outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Yen drops after BOJ votes 7-2 to hike by 25 bps
  • Traders doubt BOJ commitment to further increases
  • Dollar ticks up, oil prices cool on easing supply fears

By Saqib Iqbal Ahmed and Harry Robertson

The dollar jumped against the yen on Friday after two policymakers at the Bank of Japan dissented from a widely expected decision to raise interest rates, raising doubt among traders about the likelihood of further hikes.

The BOJ pushed rates to their highest level in 31 years at 1.25%, yet the move did not boost the Japanese currency as traders felt there was a lack of explicitly hawkish guidance.

The decision, coming on the heels of the Fed's hawkish message from earlier this week, clears the way for further dollar strength, strategists said.

"(The) lack of hiking punch makes it easier for USD to go higher," Steven Englander, head of G10 FX research at Standard Chartered, said.

"The USD strength that we have been forecasting for the medium to long term may finally be here," Englander said.

The US dollar rose 1.2% against the Japanese currency to a two-week high of 157.897 yen after wavering during BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference.

It was set for its biggest daily increase versus the yen since December and the largest weekly rally since September 2024.

"They've just clearly underwhelmed versus expectations here," said Ray Attrill, head of FX strategy at National Australia Bank in Sydney.

"And I think that one of the more staggering aspects of it was that they couldn't even get the unanimous vote for that," he said. "That really raised eyebrows in the market."

Traders remained alert to the risk of intervention to prop up the currency after Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said Tokyo won't hesitate to conduct further coordinated action, following a joint US-Japan move to boost the yen in late July.

The yen rallied sharply in early September to its highest since February as traders bet the BOJ would embark on multiple rate hikes, although those wagers came under question on Friday.

ENERGY PRICES IN FOCUS

The rally against the yen helped the US dollar index climb 0.25% to 100.48, as broader currency markets remained focused on energy prices and the US Federal Reserve.

The index, which tracks the currency against six major peers, was up 1.4% for the week to around a six-week high after the US Federal Reserve hiked interest rates on Wednesday and signalled more increases could be coming.

Traders see a roughly 55% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Fed's next two-day meeting next month, up from 27% a week ago, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Oil prices slipped to their lowest levels in around a week on signs of easing supply pressures in Saudi Arabia.

China has asked Tehran to help rein in the Iran-aligned Houthis after their military blitz on Saudi Arabia over the past week, three Iranian sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The euro fell 0.1% to $1.14595 and was set to end the week 1% lower after the Fed's rate hike.

The British pound was also 0.1% lower at $1.335, giving up earlier gains after retail sales data beat expectations on Friday. The Bank of England held interest rates on Thursday but also suggested it could raise borrowing costs.

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin rose 4% to above $80,000 on Friday — its third straight day of gains — as it extended a rebound from Tuesday's sharp selloff, when the US Senate failed to advance comprehensive cryptocurrency legislation in a setback for digital-asset companies.

data.title: NAVER D2SF Invests in AI-Driven Precision Medicine Company ImpriMed
data.description:
• ImpriMed combines ex vivo functional testing with multimodal AI to support personalized cancer treatment decisions and drug development
  • The investment is part of ImpriMed's $10 million Series A2 bridge round as the company advances U.S. commercialization and expands into Asia
  • NAVER D2SF to strengthen its global healthcare founder community through its healthcare network and go-to-market expertise

SEOUL, South Korea, Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NAVER D2SF, NAVER's inhouse corporate venture arm, has invested in ImpriMed, a Silicon Valley-based precision medicine company, joining ImpriMed's $10 million Series A2 bridge round. ImpriMed develops AI-driven precision medicine solutions that combine ex vivo analysis of patient-derived live cancer cells with genomic, immunophenotypic, and clinical data to support personalized treatment decisions. NAVER D2SF's investment reflects ImpriMed's commercial and clinical experience in the U.S. healthcare market and its growing capabilities across precision medicine and drug development.

Precision oncology increasingly relies on integrating multiple types of patient data to account for differences in disease biology and treatment response. ImpriMed applies multimodal AI to patient-specific cancer cell characteristics, drug response profiles, and clinical information to enable more personalized treatment selection.

At the core of ImpriMed's xCellSense® platform is its ability to keep patient cancer cells viable ex vivo for extended periods, enabling evaluation of their biological characteristics and drug sensitivity. The platform combines these results with immunophenotypic, genomic, and clinical data to guide treatment decisions. ImpriMed is developing AI models trained on more than 3.5 million data points, combining real-world data with functional cell analysis to improve predictive accuracy.

ImpriMed is preparing to commercialize products for blood cancers and blood infection, targeting FDA clearance and CLIA certification by Q1 2027 for an initial U.S. launch. The company has also established business partnerships with major U.S. hospitals as it builds its human health presence in North America. In South Korea, ImpriMed has developed software for multiple myeloma prognosis and therapy-response predictions. The software has been designated an Innovative Medical Device by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) and is progressing through the approval and commercialization process. ImpriMed also collaborates with leading tertiary hospitals, including Catholic University Seoul St. Mary's Hospital, Seoul Asan Medical Center, and Gangneung Asan Hospital.

ImpriMed's human healthcare expansion is supported by its commercial experience in veterinary precision oncology and its growing CRO business in drug development. In veterinary medicine, ImpriMed has performed more than 27,000 tests for canine and feline lymphoma to guide treatment decisions. A retrospective study showed a threefold increase in survival time and a fourfold improvement in treatment response, and the findings have been published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal. ImpriMed's solutions are currently used by more than 600 veterinary hospitals across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, and South Korea.

ImpriMed was co-founded in Silicon Valley by CEO Sungwon Lim and CTO Jamin Koo, who studied together at KAIST and Stanford University. The company brings together expertise in biomedical research, AI modeling, clinical collaboration, and commercialization. Beyond North America, ImpriMed plans to expand into the European and Asian markets.

The $10 million bridge round follows ImpriMed's $23 million Series A in 2023. The round was led by LB Investment, with participation from new investors NAVER D2SF, Samsung Securities, and Alois Ventures, as well as follow-on investments from existing investors BonAngels and Han River Partners.

NAVER D2SF continues to invest in healthcare startups targeting the North American market. Through NAVER D2SF's founder network, portfolio companies such as Soundable Health, PranaQ, and NubiLab share local market knowledge and operating experience, fostering collaboration across R&D and go-to-market strategy.

About NAVER D2SF

NAVER D2SF is NAVER's in-house corporate venture arm, supporting startups through investment and collaboration. Founded in 1999, NAVER has been Korea's leading search engine for more than 20 years and operates across commerce, content, fintech, and cloud services. Guided by its technology vision of D2 (For Developers, By Developers), NAVER continues to develop new technologies and build global partnerships.

To learn more, visit https://d2sf.naver.com.
